skill.name: codebase-cleanup-deps-audit
skill.description: Audit project dependencies for vulnerabilities, license compliance, maintenance risk, bundle size, and supply-chain issues with actionable remediation guidance.
skill.summary: Review dependency risk and plan secure package updates across common ecosystems.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Confirmed risk is limited to a documented auto-update shell workflow and outbound dependency lookup examples. Most static hits are false positives from markdown references, JavaScript template literals, checklist text, and safe local command examples. No prompt injection attempt or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Automated remediation examples run package manager and shell commands that can modify project files.
remediation.suggestion: Require user approval before running update commands, avoid force fixes by default, and review lockfile changes before merge.

remediation.issue: Network lookup examples can send package names and versions to public registry or advisory services.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before external lookups and offer local or private advisory sources for confidential projects.

content.value_statement: Dependency risk is hard to triage across ecosystems and manifests. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through vulnerability, license, update, and remediation reviews.
actual_capabilities: Inventories dependency manifests for npm, Python, Ruby, Java, Go, Rust, PHP, and .NET examples.
Maps packages to vulnerability, license, outdated version, bundle size, and supply-chain checks.
Prioritizes findings by severity, exposure, exploit availability, and maintenance signals.
Drafts remediation plans and pull request summaries for dependency updates.
Provides CI monitoring workflow examples for recurring dependency audits.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not include a packaged scanner binary.
It may need network access to public registries or advisory APIs.
Automated fixes can break builds and require staging validation.
Results depend on available lockfiles and package manager metadata.

use_cases.title: Release Dependency Review
use_cases.description: Audit vulnerable packages and license risks before a release freeze.

use_cases.title: Upgrade Planning
use_cases.description: Create a prioritized update plan with compatibility notes and test expectations.

use_cases.title: Continuous Monitoring Setup
use_cases.description: Design recurring dependency checks and alert workflows for shared repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Dependency Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a broad repository review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this repository for dependency security risk. Inventory manifests, identify vulnerable packages, and summarize the highest priority fixes.

prompt_templates.title: License Compliance Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Focus on legal and policy exposure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review dependency licenses for this project. Flag restrictive or unknown licenses, explain the risk, and suggest compliant alternatives where possible.

prompt_templates.title: Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn audit results into an execution plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dependency remediation plan. Group fixes by severity, note breaking-change risk, and include validation steps for each update group.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Supply Chain Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess security posture beyond known CVEs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze supply-chain risk for this project. Include maintainer activity, typosquatting signals, transitive exposure, bundle impact, and monitoring recommendations.

output_examples.input: Audit a Node and Python service before release.
output: Risk overview sorted by critical, high, medium, and low impact.
Packages needing immediate updates, with compatibility and test notes.
License issues and follow-up questions for the maintainers.

output_examples.input: Plan dependency updates for a legacy API.
output: A phased update plan that separates security fixes from routine upgrades.
Rollback guidance for lockfile changes and failed test runs.
Review checklist for the dependency update pull request.
Recommended scan cadence for package manifests and lockfiles.
Alert rules for critical vulnerabilities and policy violations.
Owner assignments for remediation and follow-up tracking.

best_practices: Run audits on an up-to-date branch with lockfiles committed.
Confirm outbound network use before checking private dependency inventories.
Test suggested upgrades in staging before merging them.
anti_patterns: Running automated fix commands without reviewing dependency changes.
Sending private package names to public services without approval.
Treating severity labels as proof of exploitability.

faq.question: Does this skill run a scanner automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides audit guidance, example workflows, and remediation structure. Tool execution still depends on user approval and environment access.

faq.question: Which ecosystems are covered?
faq.answer: The playbook includes examples for npm, Python, Ruby, Java, Go, Rust, PHP, and .NET manifests.

faq.question: Can it check license compliance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes license inventory, compliance issue grouping, and report formats for restrictive or unknown licenses.

faq.question: Can it suggest dependency upgrades?
faq.answer: Yes. It can prioritize updates, explain compatibility risk, and outline tests needed before merge.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Some examples use public advisory and registry services. Private projects should approve those lookups before sending package metadata.

faq.question: Is it suitable for confidential repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, if users avoid public lookups or use approved internal advisory sources for private dependency data.
